nodes.label: Biodegradable plastics

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Plastic waste reduction|Biodegradable plastics_qna_000
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: Why is PLA considered a popular choice in the bioplastics industry?
nodes.answer: PLA is widely used as a bioplastic due to being completely biodegradable and serving as an alternative to traditional plastics.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Plastic waste reduction|Biodegradable plastics_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How does the environmental impact of the novel biocomposite compare to its counterparts?
nodes.answer: The novel biocomposite generally has higher environmental impacts than conventional antibacterial materials like virgin PLA, fossil-based polypropylene (PP), and high-density polyethylene (HDPE).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Plastic waste reduction|Biodegradable plastics_qna_002
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What is the main motivation behind the analysis of bio-based antibacterial plastics based on PLA?
nodes.answer: The main motivation is to analyze if there is an added environmental value compared to conventional materials, which lack inherent antibacterial properties and require separate treatments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Plastic waste reduction|Biodegradable plastics_qna_003
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: How are biopolymers classified according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Biopolymers are classified into three groups based on origin and degradability: (1) bio-based and non-biodegradable, (2) bio-based and biodegradable, and (3) fossil-based and biodegradable.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Plastic waste reduction|Biodegradable plastics_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the advantages of enzymatic hydrolysis over other chemical processes for degrading PET?
nodes.answer: Enzymatic hydrolysis yields TPA and EG, the monomers used to generate new PET polymers, and follows a first-order kinetics equation, offering a sustainable approach to fabric recycling.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Plastic waste reduction|Biodegradable plastics_qna_005
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Are all natural fibres biodegradable?
nodes.answer: Yes, most natural fibres like cotton, wool, and silk are biodegradable, meaning they can break down naturally in the environment without causing harm.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Plastic waste reduction|Biodegradable plastics_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is polyester clothing a concern for plastic pollution?
nodes.answer: Clothing made from polyester fibres is non-biodegradable and can take up to 200 years to biodegrade, leading to plastic pollution. Additionally, microfibres shed from polyester clothing can enter water courses and the food chain, posing harm to the human digestive system.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Plastic waste reduction|Biodegradable plastics_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does polyester contribute to environmental pollution?
nodes.answer: Polyester fibres are non-biodegradable and can take up to 200 years to biodegrade, leading to environmental pollution. This can have long-lasting negative effects on the environment.
